title: Cities Skylines | Franklin, Episode 4: Revolution
premise: While building Fort Montresor, the presenter argues that the American Revolution largely replaced governing elites without transforming class relations; ICE preamble and grotesque Cambodia satire frame an anti-tyranny refrain.
coverage: An anti-ICE preamble leads into Fort Montresor’s construction, revolutionary class politics and a dark Cambodia satire. The closing tour compares huts with replacement houses. Historical claims are the presenter’s account; the Cambodia trip is satire, and the university name is deliberately censored.

panels.heading: Political preamble
panels.description: White ABOLISH ICE text on black, later expanded to Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Presenter introduces his contemporary political intervention.
panels.camera: Static title card; text changes between views.
panels.action: Text appears on black.

panels.heading: Clinton shorthand
panels.description: Bill Clinton holds a saxophone in a centered photograph on black.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Wry portrait selection accompanies the attribution of deportation laws to Clinton: the saxophone-playing public image replaces a solemn policy-document illustration.

panels.heading: Detention conditions
panels.description: People lie under blankets behind chain-link fencing; later ABOLISH ICE returns.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.notes: The people in the detention photograph are unidentified.

panels.heading: Mercantilism callback
panels.description: MERCANTILISM overlays settlement gameplay before the ICE slogan returns.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Game-editor view beneath large lettering.

panels.heading: Deportability disciplines labor
panels.description: List names low wages, stolen wages, unsafe conditions and unions; bottom line says BECAUSE ICE CAN DEPORT YOU AT ANY TIME.
panels.camera: Static list builds across views.
panels.action: Text lines are added.

panels.heading: Meatpacking example
panels.description: Workers handle meat on a processing line in a centered photograph.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.

panels.heading: Free trade / free labor
panels.description: Text reads "FREE TRADE" DOESN'T WORK WITHOUT FREE LABOR.
panels.camera: Static typography.
panels.action: No character action.

panels.heading: Ordinary protest: setup
panels.description: Crowd carries LET THEM IN and other pro-immigration signs.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the next armed tableau: ordinary participation is contrasted with the absurd super-soldier qualification.

panels.heading: Antifa super-soldier payoff
panels.description: Posed masked armed people behind a table with anarchist/antifascist-style flags.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Literalizes the super soldier he says viewers do not have to be; connected payoff to the ordinary protest image.
panels.notes: The photographed people and location are unidentified.

panels.heading: Philadelphia appeal
panels.description: Philadelphia podium image gains END PARS / PRELIMINARY ARRAIGNMENT REPORTING SYSTEM.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.notes: PARS means Preliminary Arraignment Reporting System; the Philadelphia mayor is Kenney.

panels.heading: Series title / build preview
panels.description: Gold FRANKLIN and A DONOTEAT SERIES over completed star fort.
panels.camera: The montage cuts from barracks to overhead views of the fort, then to black.
panels.action: Title and logo appear then fade.

panels.heading: Revolution episode setup
panels.description: Regional river map with EPISODE 4 / REVOLUTION ribbon.
panels.camera: The wide aerial map gives way to a closer view of the region.
panels.action: Map navigation establishes waterways and settlements.

panels.heading: Surviving village changes
panels.description: Canoes, shoreline and small European-style houses surrounded by forest.
panels.camera: The regional map gives way to close editor views of the village.
panels.action: Buildings and ground are selected; a cleared village site appears later.
panels.visualGag: Small European-style houses make the presenter’s tradeoff between tradition and keeping rain out visible. The later hut-to-house comparisons return to the joke.

panels.heading: Old forts, British administration
panels.description: Palisade forts, a pier and British flags.
panels.camera: Close aerial views shift between old fort, pier and another fort.
panels.action: Flags are highlighted/placed; cursor selects structures.

panels.heading: Founder portrait becomes comedy
panels.description: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia still shows Charlie Day as Charlie Kelly and Danny DeVito as Frank Reynolds in ragged colonial costumes, covering the game.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Episode 3 used the cropped Danny DeVito/Frank Reynolds portion of this It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia image as William Franklin. Episode 4 widens the same colonial-costume portrait to include Charlie Day/Charlie Kelly, again illustrating the solemn Quaker-founder explanation with sitcom characters.
panels.notes: The colonial-costume image returns from episode 3 and adds Charlie Kelly. The exact television episode is uncertain.

panels.heading: Undefended port needs defenses
panels.description: Game returns to the dense town and river mouth, then cleared fort site.
panels.camera: Wide town/river views followed by closer terrain editor.
panels.action: Terrain and placement tools prepare the site.

panels.heading: Pirate taxonomy: running-gag setup
panels.description: A PIRATE list starts SOME GUY WITH A BOAT AND A CREW and adds parrot, hook, peg leg, theft, raids and profit.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Bastion pieces are placed while the list grows.
panels.visualGag: Mock-serious accessory taxonomy sets up almost identical privateer and smuggler lists.

panels.heading: Privateer taxonomy: variation
panels.description: A PRIVATEER list repeats the boat and crew but says INFREQUENTLY HAS PARROT, HOOK FOR HAND, PEG LEG; government charter is added later.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Bastions and a gatehouse are placed under accumulating text.
panels.visualGag: Connected pirate-list payoff: privateers are only less likely to have cartoon pirate accessories; charter, not virtue, distinguishes them.

panels.heading: Smuggler taxonomy: callback
panels.description: A SMUGGLER repeats boat/crew and accessories, then illegal cargo transport, profit and independence from government.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Cursor joins angular fort-wall segments.
panels.visualGag: Third repetition completes the comic taxonomy and returns the accessories to the list.

panels.heading: Threats, tribute and stalled funding
panels.description: Star-shaped perimeter becomes enclosed; earth-colored surface replaces grass within it.
panels.camera: Overhead framing alternates wide complete outline and close bastions across views.
panels.action: Perimeter segments and ground surfaces are assembled.

panels.heading: Fort Montresor completed in revolution
panels.description: Barracks rows and gatehouse fill the fort; the caption "FORT MONTRESOR" overlays the editor, rather than being an in-game label.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Selection and placement tools change the fort layout.

panels.heading: River-facing defenses
panels.description: Plain fort-editor footage shows barracks, small sheds and perimeter roads as the presenter explains river-facing guns and clear-cut approaches.
panels.camera: The view changes between oblique and top-down angles on the fort.
panels.action: Road and prop tools adjust the interior.

panels.heading: Citadel inspiration and excess
panels.description: Aerial photograph of a real star fort overlays the editor during the Halifax/Quebec inspiration explanation.
panels.camera: Cut from the editor to a static aerial photograph.
panels.action: Still photograph; editor visible around it.
panels.notes: The star-fort photograph accompanies Halifax and Quebec inspiration; the exact site is uncertain.

panels.heading: Back to the oversized fort
panels.description: Photograph clears, returning to the fort editor and interior road/prop work as the presenter admits the scale got carried away.
panels.camera: Cut back to the editor, with changing views of the fort interior.
panels.action: Cursor adjusts interior structures and routes.

panels.heading: Bourgeois revolution / spelling aside
panels.description: "BOURGEOIS" REVOLUTION with YES I HAD TO LOOK UP HOW TO SPELL IT, DON'T @ ME.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Text overlay appears above road-building editor.

sound.text: The narrator makes a pronunciation joke on “bourgeois”, the French-derived English political term. A separate caption jokes about spelling it.

panels.visualGag: Visual-only parenthesis punctures theoretical authority with spelling trouble and online-correction joke.

panels.heading: Baby’s first left-wing history book
panels.description: Howard Zinn A PEOPLE’S HISTORY OF THE UNITED STATES cover overlays fort.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Static book cover; editor below continues.
panels.visualGag: Book cover supplies the referent for the spoken Baby’s First Left-Wing History Book joke and assigned-or-banned comparison.

panels.heading: Class grievance becomes military draft
panels.description: Barracks, paved routes and smaller buildings are adjusted while the presenter recounts wealthy revolutionary organizers and Boston draft exemptions.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Selection and placement tools change the fort layout.

panels.heading: Boston refrain
panels.description: TYRANNY IS TYRANNY, LET IT COME FROM WHOM IT MAY over fort work.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Large slogan appears then clears; terrain and buildings continue being edited.
panels.notes: The Boston slogan returns in the closing passage.

panels.heading: Property qualifications and emancipation
panels.description: Storage props and crate piles are added near the fort gate and warehouses.
panels.camera: The editor alternates between oblique and overhead views of the fort.
panels.action: Cursor adds stockpiles and moves across warehouse rows.
panels.notes: The Maryland, Dunmore and Washington claims are narrated, without reenactments.

panels.heading: Freedom rhetoric and departing Loyalists
panels.description: Crates, carts and orange-roofed warehouses fill the interior.
panels.camera: Close editor view shifts across stockpiles and warehouses.
panels.action: Storage props are selected and placed.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the following Timbukton insert: narration moves fleeing Loyalists into a fictional game-universe destination.

panels.heading: Timbukton crossover payoff
panels.description: YouTube page shows TheTimeister and Cities Skylines : Timbukton playlist, with Ep.1 Gotta Start Somewhere.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Static screenshot over game editor.
panels.visualGag: Connected payoff to Loyalist flight: their destination is another creator’s fictional city, made literal by the browser screenshot.
panels.notes: The YouTube page names Timbukton and TheTimeister.

panels.heading: Mortgages, expansion and imperialism
panels.description: Fort exterior terrain is sculpted; shoreline contours and water change around bastions.
panels.camera: Close overhead views of the shoreline alternate with wider fort views. Two abrupt sky-facing views interrupt the terrain work.
panels.action: Terrain brush changes the banks; pause menu briefly appears.

panels.heading: Class structure unchanged; alternative setup
panels.description: Wide fort and landward roads; tree group highlighted blue.
panels.camera: The view widens from the bastions to the surrounding roads.
panels.action: Road/selection tools and tree selection visible.

sound.text: The narrator repeats the pronunciation joke on “bourgeois” in “bourgeois revolution”.

panels.visualGag: Setup for the Cambodia satire: the serious elite-replacement thesis prompts an apparently obvious proletarian alternative.

panels.heading: 1976: implausible personal history
panels.description: 1976 in large white text over highlighted trees near fort.
panels.camera: Overlay is static; game viewpoint shifts from trees toward fort.
panels.action: Date appears, then disappears.
panels.visualGag: Connected Cambodia-satire setup: sudden date card lends documentary form to an implausible first-person trip.
panels.notes: The university redaction is a mock-censorship joke.

panels.heading: University affiliation: mock censorship
panels.description: UNIVERSITY OF in large white lettering ends in a solid black redaction bar over highlighted trees in the editor.
panels.camera: The UNIVERSITY OF caption and redaction bar overlay the tree-selection view.
panels.action: Black bar conceals the purported affiliation; background tree selection remains visible.
panels.visualGag: The narrator gives his implausible first-person 1976 trip a scholarly credential, then hides the institution with a mock-censorship bar.
panels.notes: The university name is deliberately hidden.

panels.heading: Back to gameplay before SDS label
panels.description: The university overlay clears, revealing the fort, roads and trees.
panels.camera: Editor viewpoint widens toward the completed fort.
panels.action: With the redaction card gone, editor work continues.
panels.visualGag: Bridge within the mock-documentary trip setup, between the censored credential and the following radical-group label.

panels.heading: Students for a Democratic Society
panels.description: STUDENTS FOR A DEMOCRATIC SOCIETY in white overlays the roads, trees and pier by the fort.
panels.camera: The group-name caption holds over the editor.
panels.action: Group-name label appears, then gives way to the Cambodia map.
panels.visualGag: Connected satirical setup: institutional and activist labels make the invented revolutionary study trip look like a sober documentary before its atrocity-apologist reversal.

panels.heading: Cambodia map
panels.description: Green Cambodia map with neighboring countries and Phnom Penh.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: The Cambodia map gives the satirical trip story the look of a documentary.

panels.heading: Pol Pot portrait
panels.description: Black-and-white Pol Pot portrait fills screen.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Connected Cambodia sequence: leader portrait formalizes the claimed revolutionary encounter.

panels.heading: Khmer Rouge flag
panels.description: Yellow temple emblem on red flag fills screen.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Rapid flag insert continues mock-documentary revolutionary setup, to be contradicted by deprivation/coercion imagery.

panels.heading: Armed arrival photograph
panels.description: Black-and-white photograph of troops and people on an armored vehicle in a street.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Connected satirical setup: military triumphal image accompanies rapid democratization language; later photographs overturn the praise.

panels.heading: Earthworks photograph
panels.description: Line of people carrying tools in a trench.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: The forced-labor image begins to expose the euphemistic praise for revolutionary activity.

panels.heading: Mass worksite photograph
panels.description: Large worksite full of laborers carrying loads, over game editor.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: The mass worksite photograph undercuts the narrator’s praise for revolutionary labor.

panels.heading: Evacuated city
panels.description: Debris-filled street with nearly empty storefronts; children stand in foreground.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Contradictory visual to the celebratory evacuation of surplus urban population; first explicit deprivation image in the reform-praise sequence.

panels.heading: Agricultural labor
panels.description: Young people with tools dig in bare earth.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: The young laborers accompany the praise for increased agricultural production, continuing the grim satire.

panels.heading: Rice economy / children with bowls
panels.description: Line of children holding bowls appears over game editor.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: The children’s empty bowls undercut the humanitarian rhetoric about abolishing currency. The joke targets that rhetoric.

panels.heading: Humane re-education contradicted
panels.description: Man points a pistol in foreground with armed men behind him.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: The armed men contradict the praise for humane re-education.

panels.heading: Compassion contradicted by skulls
panels.description: Shelves packed with human skulls overlay game editor, then gameplay returns.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Shelves of skulls contradict the claims of compassionate minority treatment. The satire targets atrocity apologetics, not the victims.

panels.heading: Tuol Sleng / atrocity photograph
panels.description: A body on a bed in a bare room is shown in a sepia-toned photograph, then the fort reappears.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: The body photograph undercuts the claim that atrocities were a small price to pay, exposing the absurdity of the narrator’s satirical trip story.

panels.heading: Combat Liberalism
panels.description: Mao Tse-tung COMBAT LIBERALISM book cover over editor.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.visualGag: Connected dark-satire payoff: book literalizes combating liberalism after the atrocity excuses.

panels.heading: ANYWAY: dismissal payoff
panels.description: Full-screen black with white ANYWAY.
panels.camera: Static full-screen card; hard cut from editor/book insert.
panels.action: No character action.
panels.visualGag: Final payoff to Cambodia sequence: grotesquely casual dismissal is made a full-screen transition before American history resumes.

panels.heading: Articles of Confederation
panels.description: ARTICLES OF CONFEDERATION heading overlays fort exterior roads.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Static document insert above continuing gameplay.
panels.visualGag: The document becomes the target of the narrator’s absolute turd and drunk libertarians insults.

panels.heading: SHAY'S REBELLION title
panels.description: SHAY'S REBELLION appears in large white letters over the fort exterior and road editor.
panels.camera: The caption holds over oblique gameplay.
panels.action: Title appears briefly while a road section is highlighted.
panels.notes: The title spells Shays’ Rebellion as “SHAY’S REBELLION”. Whether the spelling is a joke is unclear.

panels.heading: Rebellion explanation continues
panels.description: Title has cleared; editor shows the outer road network and bastion while the presenter explains farmers' grievances.
panels.camera: The overhead and oblique views shift around the fort’s approaches.
panels.action: Road tools continue modifying approaches.

panels.heading: Shays’ Rebellion and hard currency
panels.description: Landward roads, shoreline and outer fort terrain are modified.
panels.camera: Close overhead exterior views shift around perimeter.
panels.action: Terrain brush changes contours; road tools adjust approaches.

panels.heading: Egalitarian qualification: Paine
panels.description: Portrait associated by narration with Thomas Paine overlays fort.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.notes: Narration associates the portrait with Thomas Paine.

panels.heading: Banneker challenges Jefferson
panels.description: Portrait associated with Benjamin Banneker overlays fort moat, then editor returns.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static image.
panels.action: Still image; no visible moving-character action.
panels.notes: Narration associates the portrait with Benjamin Banneker.

panels.heading: Reading recommendation before payoff
panels.description: Plain editor footage shows fort walls and barracks during the recommendation of Zinn and the transition into the closing refrain.
panels.camera: The view changes from the exterior wall to the barracks.
panels.action: Game tools remain visible as the presenter finishes his recommendation.

panels.heading: Tyranny refrain returns
panels.description: TYRANNY IS TYRANNY, LET IT COME FROM WHOM IT MAY overlays the finished fort, fading darker.
panels.camera: Framing moves from barracks to wider views before fade to black.
panels.action: Slogan appears; construction montage ends.
panels.notes: The slogan repeats the Boston draft passage.

panels.heading: Village before: huts
panels.description: UI-free shoreline village with rounded huts, canoes, stumps and campfire.
panels.camera: The viewpoint changes around the shoreline settlement.
panels.action: Campfire is pictured; huts and canoes stationary.
panels.visualGag: Before-image setup for the following house reveal: rounded huts replay the traditional architecture from the earlier keeping-the-rain-out joke; the next panel supplies its delayed practical-upgrade payoff.

panels.heading: Village after: houses
panels.description: Same-looking shoreline layout now has yellow and red European-style houses behind canoes.
panels.camera: An edited before-and-after comparison continues around the village.
panels.action: The edited comparison replaces huts with houses.
panels.visualGag: The small European-style houses pay off the earlier keeping-rain-out joke. Shoreline, canoes and fire remain comparable to the hut village, and another palisaded settlement will repeat the comparison.
panels.notes: The edited hut-to-house comparison recalls the earlier keeping-rain-out joke.

panels.heading: Completed fort cinematic tour
panels.description: Finished star fort, moat, bridges, regular barracks and orange-roofed warehouses.
panels.camera: Changing views circle the fort before switching to another aerial angle.
panels.action: UI hidden; structures stationary while viewpoint moves.

panels.heading: Second village before: palisade and huts
panels.description: Palisaded circular village with rounded huts and fires beside canoes.
panels.camera: The view moves from the shoreline toward the palisaded settlement.
panels.action: Buildings stationary; fire visible.
panels.visualGag: Second before-image setup for the hut-to-house callback: the palisaded settlement still has rounded traditional huts, preparing another reveal of the practical rain-excluding houses praised in the early recap.

panels.heading: Second village after: wooden houses
panels.description: Palisade now encloses small rectangular houses, with houses also outside near boats.
panels.camera: The wooden-house reveal is followed by changing angles around the village.
panels.action: An edited comparison replaces the huts with wooden houses.
panels.visualGag: The palisaded village repeats the hut-to-house reveal, returning once more to the joke about keeping rain out.

panels.heading: Fort and river relationship
panels.description: Overhead completed fort, narrow river channel and settlements with piers on opposite banks.
panels.camera: The view shifts from the fort across the river mouth.
panels.action: Static buildings/landscape; camera viewpoint travels.

panels.heading: Gatehouse to whole fort
panels.description: Orange gatehouse and storage carts give way to barracks rows and broad fort interior.
panels.camera: Cinematic view pulls back from the gatehouse across the fort interior.
panels.action: Buildings and crates stationary.

panels.heading: Patreon credits
panels.description: My Patreons list in white on black.
panels.camera: Static credits card after fort fades darker.
panels.action: The supporter list remains fixed on black.

panels.heading: DNE token logo
panels.description: Token reads GOOD FOR / DNE / ONE FARE with diagonal red stripe on black.
panels.camera: The token appears after the credits and changes position down and right.
panels.action: Channel emblem displayed.
